title: Positive Discipline: Teaching, Not Punishing
hook: Discipline means teaching, not hurting. The AAP's most effective tools are calm consistency, catching good behavior, and clear consequences — and it advises against spanking and harsh words.
key_points: Discipline is teaching right from wrong with calm words and modeling — not punishment.
Set clear, consistent rules in age-appropriate terms, and keep them consistent across all caregivers.
Catch good behavior: notice and praise the things you want to see more of.
Use calm, immediate consequences and brief time-outs (about 1 minute per year of age); AAP advises against spanking, yelling, and shaming.
content_html: The word "discipline" really means to teach. The AAP frames effective discipline as helping a child learn right from wrong with calm words and actions — and modeling the behavior you want to see — rather than punishing. That foundation is built on clear, consistent rules explained in terms your child can understand, applied the same way by every caregiver so the limits are predictable.
extra_html: Two everyday tools do a lot of the work: catch good behavior and name it ("you put your toys away — nice job"), and when misbehavior happens, calmly and firmly follow through with a consequence that fits. A brief time-out — roughly one minute per year of age, after a warning — gives everyone a chance to reset. The AAP advises against spanking, yelling, and shaming: research shows they don't work well and can harm a child's long-term physical and mental health. This is general educational information from the AAP — for persistent behavior concerns, your pediatrician can help.

source.name: HealthyChildren.org (AAP) — What's the Best Way to Discipline My Child?

related.title: Why Toddlers Have Tantrums
related.hook: Tantrums are a normal part of toddler development — big feelings hitting a brain that can't yet manage them or fully put them into words.

related.title: Potty Training: Readiness Over Age
related.hook: There's no magic age to potty train. Readiness signs matter far more — and a calm, child-led, pressure-free approach beats pushing a child who isn't ready yet.

flashcards.prompt: What does the AAP say about spanking and harsh verbal punishment?

choices.text: It advises against them — they don't work well and can be harmful
It recommends them for serious misbehavior
It says they're fine as long as they're rare

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP advises against spanking, yelling, and shaming. They're ineffective and can harm a child's long-term physical and mental health.

flashcards.prompt: What's a rule of thumb for time-out length?
flashcards.back_html: About 1 minute per year of age. Warn first, briefly explain what the child did wrong, and stay calm — time-out is a reset, not a punishment.
